Shapes and text

7 calls on gfx, generated from the firmware. Every one exists on the device exactly as written here.

The whole no-assets surface. Every app can call these, and many of the best ones in the library call nothing else.

gfx.circle

gfx.circle(x, y, r, color [, filled])

(x,y) is the CENTRE, not a corner like gfx.rect. filled defaults to false. A negative radius draws nothing; a float radius is floored, so a sin()-driven pulse is safe.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3rrequired
4colorrequired
5filledoptional, default false

gfx.clear

gfx.clear(color)

Fill the whole canvas with one palette index, and mark the shared depth buffer for reset. Nearly every draw starts here; without it the previous frame shows through wherever this one draws nothing. Index 0 is the one to choose deliberately: it is the sky, the water, the room the game happens in.

#argument
1colorrequired

gfx.line

gfx.line(x1, y1, x2, y2, color)

Bresenham, inclusive endpoints, clipped per pixel, so coordinates off the canvas are safe rather than fatal.

#argument
1x1required
2y1required
3x2required
4y2required
5colorrequired

gfx.rect

gfx.rect(x, y, w, h, color [, filled])

(x,y) is the top-left corner. filled defaults to FALSE, so the plain five-argument call draws an outline; this is the most common surprise in a first app.

#argument
1xrequired
2yrequired
3wrequired
4hrequired
5colorrequired
6filledoptional, default false

gfx.text

gfx.text(str, x, y, color [, size])

engine v8

Size 1, 2 or 3 (default 1), and each size is its OWN glyph set rather than a scale: 4x6, 8x12 and 12x18 cells, so big text is drawn at its own resolution instead of upscaled. Advance is always 4*size px per character and line height 6*size px, so centre with x = (gfx.w - #str * 4 * size) / 2. Do the arithmetic, do not eyeball it. "\n" starts a new line.

ASCII 32..127 ONLY. Every other byte draws a literal "?", which bites hardest exactly where it is most tempting: a star, an arrow, a heart or an accented name in a score badge. "★ 70" renders as "?70?" because the star is three bytes. Draw those with gfx.circle / gfx.tri / gfx.rect.

Anything a CHILD reads wants size 3 (size 2 for secondary labels); size 1 is a 4x6 glyph, genuinely unreadable to a five-year-old, and exists for debug text. Size 3 needs engine v8 and clamps to 2 below that.

#argument
1strrequired
2xrequired
3yrequired
4colorrequired
5sizeoptional, default 1

gfx.tri

gfx.tri(x0,y0,x1,y1,x2,y2,color)

engine v5

flat-shaded triangle (engine v5), any winding, clipped. Lighting = the app picking a darker palette tier.

#argument
1x0required
2y0required
3x1required
4y1required
5x2required
6y2required
7colorrequired
